questions.subject: Unit 3 • The Union Executive and Parliament
questions.question: Under the Constitution of India, who has the final authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill, and for how long may the Rajya Sabha hold it?
options: The President of India; up to 14 days
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha; up to 14 days
The Union Finance Minister; up to 30 days
The Minister of Parliamentary Affairs; up to 14 days
questions.explanation: Article 110(3) provides that if a question arises about whether a Bill is a Money Bill, the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is final. A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the President's recommendation. After the Lok Sabha passes it, the Rajya Sabha may make recommendations and must return it within 14 days; otherwise, it is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Lok Sabha.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Verify procedural wording against the current official Constitution text.

questions.subject: Unit 3 • Parliamentary Committees
questions.question: Which of the following standing financial committees of Parliament has 30 members, all elected exclusively from the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all drawn from the Lok Sabha. Members are elected annually according to the prescribed proportional-representation procedure, and the Rajya Sabha has no representation on this committee. By contrast, the Public Accounts Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings have members from both Houses. The membership figures should be checked against current Lok Sabha rules and committee information.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Cross-check membership numbers against current Parliament resources.

questions.subject: Unit 3 • The Judiciary (Supreme Court and High Courts)
questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution may the President of India seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion on a question of law or fact of public importance?
questions.explanation: Article 143 empowers the President to refer certain questions of law or fact to the Supreme Court for its opinion. The Court's opinion under this advisory jurisdiction is not binding on the President in the same way as a judgment resolving a dispute. Article 131 concerns the Court's original jurisdiction, Article 137 its power to review judgments, and Article 142 its power to pass orders necessary to do complete justice.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Verify details about bench composition and the scope of Article 143 against a constitutional-law reference.

questions.subject: Unit 3 • Constitutional Bodies (Election Commission and CAG)
questions.question: Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, who is the third member of the selection committee, alongside the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha?
options: A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha
questions.verificationSource: Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023
questions.explanation: Under the 2023 Act, the selection committee comprises the Prime Minister as chairperson, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the largest opposition party where applicable), and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. The committee recommends appointments of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners to the President.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Verify the Act's exact statutory wording and any later amendments.

questions.subject: Unit 3 • Centre–State Relations and Administrative Reforms
questions.question:
Arrange the following commissions and committees on Centre–State relations in chronological order of their establishment, from earliest to latest.
1. Sarkaria Commission
2. Rajamannar Committee
3. Punchhi Commission
4. First Administrative Reforms Commission
Choose the correct code:
questions.verificationSource: Inter-State Council Secretariat, Ministry of Home Affairs
questions.explanation: The First Administrative Reforms Commission was established in January 1966 (4). The Tamil Nadu government appointed the Rajamannar Committee in 1969 (2). The Sarkaria Commission was constituted in 1983 (1), and the Commission on Centre–State Relations chaired by Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi was constituted in 2007 (3). The correct order is 4 – 2 – 1 – 3.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Verify exact establishment dates from official commission records.

questions.subject: Unit 3 • Panchayati Raj and Local Government
questions.question: Which Article, inserted into Part IX by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, provides for the Governor to constitute a State Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats?
questions.verificationSource: Constitution of India, Part IX, Articles 243I and 243K
questions.explanation: Article 243I provides for the Governor to constitute a State Finance Commission at the expiry of every fifth year to review the financial position of Panchayats and make recommendations on the distribution of certain revenues. Article 243K concerns elections to Panchayats, Article 243D addresses reservation of seats, and Article 243G concerns the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Check the exact constitutional wording and numbering against the official Constitution text.

questions.subject: Unit 3 • Public Policy, Good Governance and the Right to Information
questions.question: Under Section 7(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, within what period must information be provided when the request concerns a person's life or liberty?
questions.explanation: Section 7(1) generally requires a Public Information Officer to respond within 30 days of receiving a request. Its proviso requires information concerning the life or liberty of a person to be provided within 48 hours. The Act's other timelines may vary in particular procedural circumstances, so the statutory text should be consulted for exceptions.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Check the statutory proviso and exact timeline against the Act.

questions.subject: Unit 3 • Lokpal and Lokayuktas
questions.question: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, how many members may the Lokpal have in addition to its Chairperson, and what minimum proportion must be Judicial Members?
options: Up to 6 members; at least 33% Judicial Members
Up to 10 members; at least 50% Judicial Members
Up to 8 members; at least 50% Judicial Members
Up to 5 members; at least 50% Judicial Members
questions.explanation: Section 3 provides for a Lokpal consisting of a Chairperson and up to eight members. At least 50% of the members must be Judicial Members. The Act also contains requirements concerning representation among members from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, minorities and women. The detailed statutory language should be checked directly before publication.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Confirm the membership composition and statutory wording against the current Act.

questions.subject: Unit 3 • Rights Issues and Commissions
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) and inserted Article 338B?
questions.verificationSource: Constitution of India and the 89th and 102nd Constitutional Amendment Acts
questions.explanation: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018 gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes and inserted Article 338B. It also inserted Article 342A concerning the specification of socially and educationally backward classes. The 105th Amendment later restored the power of States and Union Territories to prepare and maintain their own lists of socially and educationally backward classes within the constitutional framework.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Confirm amendment details against the official amendment text.

questions.subject: Unit 3 • International Organisations and the United Nations
questions.question: Which of the six principal organs of the United Nations is headquartered in The Hague, the Netherlands, rather than in New York City?
questions.verificationSource: Charter of the United Nations, Chapter XIV
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice, the UN's principal judicial organ, is based at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands. The other principal UN organs are based at UN headquarters in New York, though some meetings and offices may be located elsewhere. The ICJ has 15 judges elected for nine-year terms by the General Assembly and Security Council.
questions.reviewStatus: Translation draft. Confirm institutional wording and headquarters from official UN sources.
